title: Participle clauses
note: -ing clauses for time and for reason (incl. Not + -ing) · past participle clauses with passive meaning · Having / Having been + past participle for an earlier action · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 8)

items.en: Walking to the station, I met my neighbour.
items.cz: Když jsem šel na nádraží, potkal jsem souseda.
items.gap: ____ to the station, I met my neighbour.
accepts: Walking to the station, I met my neighbour.
items.explanation: -ing clause for time: same subject, so 'when I' disappears and the -ing form is left.
items.explanation_cz: -ing věta pro čas: stejný podmět, takže „když já“ zmizí a zůstane -ing tvar.

items.en: Leaving the office, she closed the window.
items.cz: Když odcházela z kanceláře, zavřela okno.
items.gap: ____ the office, she closed the window.
accepts: Leaving the office, she closed the window.
items.explanation: The -ing clause comes first and a comma separates it from the main clause.
items.explanation_cz: -ing věta stojí vpředu a od hlavní věty ji odděluje čárka.

items.en: Waiting on the platform, we read the newspaper.
items.cz: Zatímco jsme čekali na nástupišti, četli jsme noviny.
items.gap: ____ on the platform, we read the newspaper.
accepts: Waiting on the platform, we read the newspaper.
items.explanation: Two actions at the same time: the longer one goes in the -ing clause.
items.explanation_cz: Dva děje současně: ten delší jde do -ing věty.

items.en: Opening the letter, he found a ticket.
items.cz: Když otevřel dopis, našel lístek.
items.gap: ____ the letter, he found a ticket.
accepts: Opening the letter, he found a ticket.
items.explanation: -ing also works for one action straight after another.
items.explanation_cz: -ing funguje i pro děj těsně následující po druhém.

items.en: Driving to the airport, we listened to the news.
items.cz: Cestou na letiště jsme poslouchali zprávy.
items.gap: ____ to the airport, we listened to the news.
accepts: Driving to the airport, we listened to the news.
items.explanation: The -ing form never shows tense — the main verb does that.
items.explanation_cz: -ing tvar nikdy neukazuje čas — ten určuje sloveso v hlavní větě.

items.en: Sitting in the garden, she wrote two letters.
items.cz: Když seděla na zahradě, napsala dva dopisy.
items.gap: ____ in the garden, she wrote two letters.
accepts: Sitting in the garden, she wrote two letters.
items.explanation: Both clauses share one subject: she. That is the condition for a participle clause.
items.explanation_cz: Obě věty mají jeden podmět: she. To je podmínka participiální vazby.

items.en: Standing at the window, he looked at the street.
items.cz: Když stál u okna, díval se na ulici.
items.gap: ____ at the window, he looked at the street.
accepts: Standing at the window, he looked at the street.
items.explanation: Not 'Stood at the window' — the active -ing form is needed here.
items.explanation_cz: Ne „Stood at the window“ — je potřeba činný -ing tvar.

items.en: Entering the restaurant, we looked for a free table.
items.cz: Když jsme vešli do restaurace, hledali jsme volný stůl.
items.gap: ____ the restaurant, we looked for a free table.
accepts: Entering the restaurant, we looked for a free table.
items.explanation: The participle clause replaces a whole 'when …' clause.
items.explanation_cz: Participiální vazba nahrazuje celou větu s „when …“.

items.en: Reading the contract, she found a mistake.
items.cz: Když četla smlouvu, našla chybu.
items.gap: ____ the contract, she found a mistake.
accepts: Reading the contract, she found a mistake.
items.explanation: Written English uses this to keep two short clauses in one sentence.
items.explanation_cz: Psaná angličtina tím spojí dvě krátké věty do jedné.

items.en: Running to the platform, I dropped my keys.
items.cz: Když jsem běžel na nástupiště, upustil jsem klíče.
items.gap: ____ to the platform, I dropped my keys.
accepts: Running to the platform, I dropped my keys.
items.explanation: The subject of the -ing clause must be the subject of the main clause.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět -ing věty musí být podmětem hlavní věty.

items.en: Checking the report, the manager found two problems.
items.cz: Když manažer kontroloval zprávu, našel dva problémy.
items.gap: ____ the report, the manager found two problems.
accepts: Checking the report, the manager found two problems.
items.explanation: The subject can come later, in the main clause — it still governs the -ing form.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět může přijít až v hlavní větě — i tak řídí -ing tvar.

items.en: Travelling to Brno, we stopped in a small village.
items.cz: Cestou do Brna jsme se zastavili v malé vesnici.
items.gap: ____ to Brno, we stopped in a small village.
accepts: Travelling to Brno, we stopped in a small village.
Traveling to Brno, we stopped in a small village.
items.explanation: British spelling doubles the l: travelling. US English writes traveling.
items.explanation_cz: Britský pravopis zdvojuje l: travelling. Americká angličtina píše traveling.

items.en: Feeling tired, we stopped for coffee.
items.cz: Protože jsme byli unavení, zastavili jsme se na kávu.
items.gap: ____ tired, we stopped for coffee.
accepts: Feeling tired, we stopped for coffee.
items.explanation: The same -ing clause also gives a reason: 'because we felt tired'.
items.explanation_cz: Stejná -ing věta vyjadřuje i důvod: „protože jsme byli unavení“.

items.en: Knowing the manager well, she asked for a meeting.
items.cz: Protože manažera dobře znala, požádala o schůzku.
items.gap: ____ the manager well, she asked for a meeting.
accepts: Knowing the manager well, she asked for a meeting.
items.explanation: State verbs work here too, even though they take no continuous tense.
items.explanation_cz: Fungují tu i stavová slovesa, přestože nemají průběhový čas.

items.en: Not knowing the address, I called my colleague.
items.cz: Protože jsem neznal adresu, zavolal jsem kolegovi.
items.gap: ____ knowing the address, I called my colleague.
accepts: Not knowing the address, I called my colleague.
items.explanation: The negative goes in front of the -ing form: Not knowing… Never 'Don't knowing'.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor stojí před -ing tvarem: Not knowing… Nikdy „Don't knowing“.

items.en: Not having a passport, she could not travel.
items.cz: Protože neměla pas, nemohla cestovat.
items.gap: Not ____ a passport, she could not travel.
accepts: Not having a passport, she could not travel.
items.explanation: have becomes having after Not, like any other verb.
items.explanation_cz: have se po Not mění na having, stejně jako každé jiné sloveso.

items.en: Living near the office, she walks to work.
items.cz: Protože bydlí blízko kanceláře, chodí do práce pěšky.
items.gap: ____ near the office, she walks to work.
accepts: Living near the office, she walks to work.
Living near the office, he walks to work.
items.explanation: The main clause can be present — the -ing form fits any tense.
items.explanation_cz: Hlavní věta může být v přítomném čase — -ing tvar se hodí ke každému času.

items.en: Wanting a better price, they visited three shops.
items.cz: Protože chtěli lepší cenu, obešli tři obchody.
items.gap: ____ a better price, they visited three shops.
accepts: Wanting a better price, they visited three shops.
items.explanation: Reason first, result second — the usual order in writing.
items.explanation_cz: Nejdřív důvod, pak výsledek — obvyklé pořadí v psaném projevu.

items.en: Needing more money, he took a second job.
items.cz: Protože potřeboval víc peněz, vzal si druhou práci.
items.gap: ____ more money, he took a second job.
accepts: Needing more money, he took a second job.
items.explanation: This is 'because he needed', compressed into two words.
items.explanation_cz: Je to „because he needed“ stlačené do dvou slov.

items.en: Being new in the company, he asked for help.
items.cz: Protože byl ve firmě nový, požádal o pomoc.
items.gap: ____ new in the company, he asked for help.
accepts: Being new in the company, he asked for help.
items.explanation: be becomes Being, not Been, at the start of the clause.
items.explanation_cz: be se na začátku věty mění na Being, ne Been.

items.en: Working in a hotel, she meets a lot of people.
items.cz: Protože pracuje v hotelu, potkává spoustu lidí.
items.gap: ____ in a hotel, she meets a lot of people.
accepts: Working in a hotel, she meets a lot of people.
Working in a hotel, he meets a lot of people.
items.explanation: Nothing marks the reason explicitly — the comma and the order carry it.
items.explanation_cz: Důvod není označen slovem — nese ho čárka a pořadí vět.

items.en: Missing the last train, we stayed in a hotel.
items.cz: Protože nám ujel poslední vlak, přespali jsme v hotelu.
items.gap: ____ the last train, we stayed in a hotel.
accepts: Missing the last train, we stayed in a hotel.
items.explanation: -ing here means the reason happened first, not at the same time.
items.explanation_cz: -ing tu znamená, že důvod nastal dřív, ne současně.

items.en: Using an old laptop, he works slowly.
items.cz: Protože používá starý notebook, pracuje pomalu.
items.gap: ____ an old laptop, he works slowly.
accepts: Using an old laptop, he works slowly.
Using an old laptop, she works slowly.
items.explanation: Used would be passive: 'a used laptop' is a laptop somebody used.
items.explanation_cz: Used by bylo trpné: „a used laptop“ je notebook, který někdo používal.

items.en: Not speaking Czech, the client brought a colleague to the meeting.
items.cz: Protože klient neuměl česky, vzal si na schůzku kolegu.
items.gap: ____ speaking Czech, the client brought a colleague to the meeting.
accepts: Not speaking Czech, the client brought a colleague to the meeting.
items.explanation: Not + -ing is the only negative form of a participle clause.
items.explanation_cz: Not + -ing je jediný záporný tvar participiální vazby.

items.en: Shocked by the news, she called her sister.
items.cz: Šokovaná tou zprávou zavolala sestře.
items.gap: ____ by the news, she called her sister.
accepts: Shocked by the news, she called her sister.
items.explanation: The past participle is passive: the news shocked her, not the other way round.
items.explanation_cz: Příčestí minulé je trpné: zpráva šokovala ji, ne naopak.

items.en: Built in 1900, the house needs repairs.
items.cz: Dům postavený v roce 1900 potřebuje opravy.
items.gap: ____ in 1900, the house needs repairs.
accepts: Built in 1900, the house needs repairs.
items.explanation: Somebody built the house — the house did not build. So: past participle.
items.explanation_cz: Dům někdo postavil — dům nestavěl. Proto příčestí minulé.

items.en: Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.
items.cz: Kniha napsaná jednoduchou angličtinou se čte snadno.
items.gap: ____ in simple English, the book is easy to read.
accepts: Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.
items.explanation: Writing here would mean the book writes something.
items.explanation_cz: Writing by tu znamenalo, že kniha něco píše.

items.en: Delayed by the rain, the train arrived late.
items.cz: Vlak, zdržený deštěm, přijel pozdě.
items.gap: ____ by the rain, the train arrived late.
accepts: Delayed by the rain, the train arrived late.
items.explanation: by + the cause is common after a past participle clause.
items.explanation_cz: Po participiální vazbě s příčestím minulým se často pojí by + příčina.

items.en: Repaired last year, the bridge is safe now.
items.cz: Most, opravený loni, je teď bezpečný.
items.gap: ____ last year, the bridge is safe now.
accepts: Repaired last year, the bridge is safe now.
items.explanation: The clause says what was done to the subject, and when.
items.explanation_cz: Vazba říká, co se s podmětem stalo a kdy.

items.en: Surprised by the price, we left the shop.
items.cz: Překvapeni cenou jsme z obchodu odešli.
items.gap: ____ by the price, we left the shop.
accepts: Surprised by the price, we left the shop.
items.explanation: -ed describes how we felt; -ing would describe the price.
items.explanation_cz: -ed popisuje, jak jsme se cítili; -ing by popisovalo cenu.

items.en: Seen from the bridge, the city looks small.
items.cz: Z mostu vypadá město malé.
items.gap: ____ from the bridge, the city looks small.
accepts: Seen from the bridge, the city looks small.
items.explanation: A past participle clause can set a viewpoint: 'if you see it from…'.
items.explanation_cz: Vazba s příčestím minulým může určit pohled: „když se na to díváte z…“.

items.en: Printed on old paper, the letter was hard to read.
items.cz: Dopis vytištěný na starém papíře se četl špatně.
items.gap: ____ on old paper, the letter was hard to read.
accepts: Printed on old paper, the letter was hard to read.
items.explanation: No 'which was' is needed — the participle carries it.
items.explanation_cz: Není třeba „which was“ — nese to příčestí.

items.en: Signed by both managers, the contract went to the client.
items.cz: Smlouva podepsaná oběma manažery šla ke klientovi.
items.gap: ____ by both managers, the contract went to the client.
accepts: Signed by both managers, the contract went to the client.
items.explanation: This is the short form of 'The contract, which was signed by…'.
items.explanation_cz: Je to zkrácená podoba „The contract, which was signed by…“.

items.en: Painted last month, the kitchen looks bigger.
items.cz: Kuchyň, vymalovaná minulý měsíc, vypadá větší.
items.gap: ____ last month, the kitchen looks bigger.
accepts: Painted last month, the kitchen looks bigger.
items.explanation: Painting the kitchen would be the action; painted is the result on the kitchen.
items.explanation_cz: Painting by byla činnost; painted je výsledek na kuchyni.

items.en: Trained in London, she works as a doctor now.
items.cz: Vyškolená v Londýně teď pracuje jako doktorka.
items.gap: ____ in London, she works as a doctor now.
accepts: Trained in London, she works as a doctor now.
items.explanation: Somebody trained her: the participle looks back at that.
items.explanation_cz: Někdo ji vyškolil: příčestí odkazuje zpět na to.

items.en: Stolen from the office, the laptop was never found.
items.cz: Notebook ukradený z kanceláře se nikdy nenašel.
items.gap: ____ from the office, the laptop was never found.
accepts: Stolen from the office, the laptop was never found.
items.explanation: Irregular verbs use the third form here: steal - stole - stolen.
items.explanation_cz: Nepravidelná slovesa tu mají třetí tvar: steal - stole - stolen.

items.en: Having finished the report, he went home.
items.cz: Když dokončil zprávu, šel domů.
items.gap: ____ finished the report, he went home.
accepts: Having finished the report, he went home.
items.explanation: Having + past participle marks the earlier of two actions.
items.explanation_cz: Having + příčestí minulé označuje dřívější ze dvou dějů.

items.en: Having checked the contract, she signed it.
items.cz: Poté co smlouvu zkontrolovala, podepsala ji.
items.gap: Having ____ the contract, she signed it.
accepts: Having checked the contract, she signed it.
items.explanation: After Having the verb takes its third form, never the -ing form.
items.explanation_cz: Po Having má sloveso třetí tvar, nikdy ne -ing.

items.en: Having missed the train, we waited an hour.
items.cz: Protože nám ujel vlak, čekali jsme hodinu.
items.gap: Having ____ the train, we waited an hour.
accepts: Having missed the train, we waited an hour.
items.explanation: Having also gives a reason, when the reason came first.
items.explanation_cz: Having vyjadřuje i důvod, pokud nastal dřív.

items.en: Having been warned, he was more careful.
items.cz: Poté co ho varovali, byl opatrnější.
items.gap: Having ____ warned, he was more careful.
accepts: Having been warned, he was more careful.
items.explanation: Having been + past participle is the passive version: somebody warned him.
items.explanation_cz: Having been + příčestí minulé je trpná varianta: někdo ho varoval.

items.en: Having lived in Prague for years, she knows the city well.
items.cz: Protože v Praze žije roky, zná to město dobře.
items.gap: ____ lived in Prague for years, she knows the city well.
accepts: Having lived in Prague for years, she knows the city well.
Having lived in Prague for years, he knows the city well.
items.explanation: Having covers a period running up to now, like the present perfect.
items.explanation_cz: Having pokrývá dobu trvající až doteď, jako předpřítomný čas.

items.en: Having written the letter, he closed the laptop.
items.cz: Když dopis napsal, zavřel notebook.
items.gap: Having ____ the letter, he closed the laptop.
accepts: Having written the letter, he closed the laptop.
items.explanation: wrote is the past simple; after Having you need written.
items.explanation_cz: wrote je minulý čas prostý; po Having je potřeba written.

items.en: Having been repaired, the car works well now.
items.cz: Poté co ho opravili, auto teď dobře funguje.
items.gap: Having been ____, the car works well now.
accepts: Having been repaired, the car works well now.
items.explanation: The car did not repair anything, so the passive form is required.
items.explanation_cz: Auto nic neopravilo, proto je nutný trpný tvar.

items.en: Having seen the film, we did not want to see it again.
items.cz: Protože jsme ten film už viděli, nechtěli jsme ho vidět znovu.
items.gap: Having ____ the film, we did not want to see it again.
accepts: Having seen the film, we did not want to see it again.
items.explanation: see - saw - seen: the third form follows Having.
items.explanation_cz: see - saw - seen: po Having jde třetí tvar.

items.en: Having taken the wrong train, they arrived very late.
items.cz: Protože si vzali špatný vlak, dorazili velmi pozdě.
items.gap: Having ____ the wrong train, they arrived very late.
accepts: Having taken the wrong train, they arrived very late.
items.explanation: take - took - taken. took would be wrong after Having.
items.explanation_cz: take - took - taken. took by po Having bylo špatně.

items.en: Having been invited, we arrived at seven.
items.cz: Protože nás pozvali, dorazili jsme v sedm.
items.gap: Having been ____, we arrived at seven.
accepts: Having been invited, we arrived at seven.
items.explanation: Regular verbs look the same in past simple and third form: invited.
items.explanation_cz: Pravidelná slovesa mají stejný tvar pro minulý čas i třetí tvar: invited.

items.en: Having studied in London, he speaks very good English.
items.cz: Protože studoval v Londýně, mluví velmi dobře anglicky.
items.gap: ____ studied in London, he speaks very good English.
accepts: Having studied in London, he speaks very good English.
items.explanation: Being studied would mean somebody studied him.
items.explanation_cz: Being studied by znamenalo, že někdo studoval jeho.

items.en: Having been closed for a year, the museum opens in May.
items.cz: Muzeum, které bylo rok zavřené, se otevírá v květnu.
items.gap: Having been ____ for a year, the museum opens in May.
accepts: Having been closed for a year, the museum opens in May.
items.explanation: Having been + past participle works for a state that lasted, too.
items.explanation_cz: Having been + příčestí minulé funguje i pro stav, který trval.

cards.title: One subject, two clauses, no conjunction
cards.title_cz: Jeden podmět, dvě věty, žádná spojka
cards.body: A participle clause cuts **when / while / because** and the subject out of the first clause and leaves a participle. It is only possible when **both clauses share the same subject** — that is the whole rule, and the source of nearly every mistake.
cards.body_cz: Participiální vazba vyškrtne z první věty **when / while / because** i podmět a nechá jen příčestí. Je možná **jen když mají obě věty stejný podmět** — to je celé pravidlo a zdroj skoro všech chyb.

table.caption: Full clause to participle clause
rows: When I walked to the station, I met my neighbour.
**Walking** to the station, I met my neighbour.
Because she felt tired, she stopped for coffee.
**Feeling** tired, she stopped for coffee.
The house, which was built in 1900, needs repairs.
**Built** in 1900, the house needs repairs.
After he had finished the report, he went home.
**Having finished** the report, he went home.

cards.title: -ing or past participle? Ask who does the action
cards.title_cz: -ing, nebo příčestí minulé? Ptejte se, kdo činnost dělá
cards.body: The choice is never about time — it is about **direction**. If the subject **does** the action, use **-ing**. If the action is **done to** the subject, use the **past participle** (the third form). This is the same test as -ed/-ing adjectives at A2, applied to a whole clause.
cards.body_cz: Volba není o čase, ale o **směru**. Pokud podmět činnost **dělá**, použijte **-ing**. Pokud se činnost **děje jemu**, použijte **příčestí minulé** (třetí tvar). Je to stejný test jako u -ed/-ing přídavných jmen na A2, jen na celou větu.
points: **Shocking** news → the news does it. **Shocked** by the news, she called her sister.
**Reading** the contract, she found a mistake. (she reads)
**Written** in simple English, the book is easy to read. (somebody wrote it)
Never: *Shocking by the news, she called her sister.*

cards.title: Time, reason — and the negative
cards.body: The same -ing form covers **two actions at once**, **one straight after another**, and **because**. English does not mark which one — the reader takes it from the sense. The negative is simply **Not** in front, and nothing else works.
cards.body_cz: Stejný -ing tvar pokrývá **dva děje současně**, **jeden hned po druhém** i **protože**. Angličtina nerozlišuje který — čtenář to pozná z významu. Zápor je prostě **Not** vpředu a nic jiného nefunguje.
points: At the same time: Waiting on the platform, we read the newspaper.
One after the other: Opening the letter, he found a ticket.
Reason: Needing more money, he took a second job.
Negative: **Not** knowing the address, I called my colleague.

cards.title: Having + third form: the earlier action
cards.body: When the first action clearly finished **before** the second, use **Having + past participle**. If the subject had the action **done to it**, add **been**: **Having been + past participle**. After *Having* the verb is always the third form — never the past simple, never -ing.
cards.body_cz: Když první děj jasně skončil **před** druhým, použijte **Having + příčestí minulé**. Pokud se děj podmětu **stal**, přidejte **been**: **Having been + příčestí minulé**. Po *Having* je sloveso vždy ve třetím tvaru — nikdy minulý čas prostý, nikdy -ing.
points: Having **finished** the report, he went home.
Having **been** warned, he was more careful.
Never: *Having wrote the letter* · *Having writing the letter*
Plain -ing is enough when the order is already obvious.

rows: **Walked** to the station, I met my neighbour.
**Walking** to the station, I met my neighbour.
**Don't** knowing the address, I called my colleague.
**Not** knowing the address, I called my colleague.
**Building** in 1900, the house needs repairs.
**Built** in 1900, the house needs repairs.
Having **wrote** the letter, he closed the laptop.
Having **written** the letter, he closed the laptop.
**Been** new in the company, he asked for help.
**Being** new in the company, he asked for help.
Waiting on the platform, **the newspaper** was interesting.
Waiting on the platform, **we** read the newspaper.
